differences.title: 1. RENDERING ENGINE
differences.leftDesc: Flutter draws its UI directly to the screen using the Skia graphics engine, ensuring pixel-perfect consistency across platforms.
differences.rightDesc: React Native utilizes native UI components provided by the OS, leading to a truly native look and feel but can vary slightly.

differences.title: 2. LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: Flutter uses Dart, a strongly-typed, AOT-compiled language optimized for UI development, offering excellent performance and tooling.
differences.rightDesc: React Native leverages JavaScript or TypeScript, allowing web developers to transition easily and use existing JS libraries.

differences.title: 3. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Flutter compiles to native ARM code and doesn't rely on a JavaScript bridge, communicating directly with its rendering engine.
differences.rightDesc: React Native uses a JavaScript bridge to communicate with native modules, which can sometimes introduce performance bottlenecks.

differences.title: 4. UI WIDGETS
differences.leftDesc: Flutter provides its own rich set of Material Design and Cupertino widgets that are rendered by Skia.
differences.rightDesc: React Native maps to the platform's native UI elements, providing a platform-specific look and feel.

differences.title: 5. HOT RELOAD
differences.leftDesc: Flutter's stateful hot reload injects updated code into the running VM, preserving app state and enabling rapid iteration.
differences.rightDesc: React Native's Fast Refresh also provides quick feedback, updating modules without losing component state.

differences.title: 6. COMMUNITY & Ecosystem
differences.leftDesc: Flutter's ecosystem is rapidly expanding with many packages and strong community support from Google.
differences.rightDesc: React Native benefits from the vast JavaScript ecosystem and a large, established community from Facebook.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Flutter's AOT compilation and direct Skia rendering often yield performance very close to native applications.
differences.rightDesc: React Native offers good performance, but the JS bridge can be a consideration for highly intensive tasks.
